name: tinySQL
tagline: Tiny 1990s pure-Java SQL engine and JDBC driver over dBase (DBF) and text files; unmaintained since 2007.
description: tinySQL is a lightweight SQL engine written entirely in Java, first shipped with Brian Jepson's 1996 book Java Database Programming. It parses a subset of SQL (SELECT with simple joins, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE/ALTER/DROP TABLE) and executes it against xBase DBF files or flat text files, exposing everything through its own JDBC driver and a small command-line client. It was never meant to be fast; its value was showing how a SQL layer and a JDBC driver can sit on top of non-SQL data. The project moved to SourceForge in 2003 under Davis Swan; the last release, 2.26, dates from March 2007.
statusNote: Last release 2.26 (March 2007) on SourceForge; no maintenance since. Use H2, HSQLDB or SQLite for embedded SQL.
developer: Brian Jepson, later maintained by Davis Swan

scale.notes: Toy-scale; no query optimisation and limited WHERE support (AND only).

strengths: Very small, readable Java codebase showing how a SQL parser and JDBC driver fit together
Reads and writes dBase DBF files that spreadsheets of its era could open
Architecture lets you put a SQL front end over non-SQL sources such as text files
weaknesses: Abandoned since 2007; targets very old Java versions
Partial SQL: WHERE supports only AND, joins were documented as buggy on dBase files
No locking, transactions or indexes worth relying on
useCases: Studying a minimal SQL engine and JDBC driver implementation
Reading legacy DBF files from old Java code
